hints.title: Minimax Game State Inversion
hints.text: A player has a winning strategy from the current state if there exists at least one legal move that places the opponent into an inescapable losing state.

hints.title: Recursive Search with Memoization
hints.text: For every adjacent pair of plus signs, flip them to minus signs and evaluate whether the opponent can win from the resulting board configuration.

hints.title: Top-Down Memoized State Evaluation
hints.text: Use a map to store outcome for state string. Iterate through index i from 0 to len - 2. If substring s[i:i+2] equals ++, recurse on flipped state. If recursive call returns false, current player wins.

complexity.notes: Optimal minimax game tree search with memoization pruning overlapping board partitions.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unmemoized minimax tree repeatedly solves identical subgames, leading to super-exponential branching.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Memoizing game states stores previously decided configurations in O(N) space per entry.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should articulate the minimax condition: winning means forcing the next player to have zero winning responses.
